findings.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 (CVSS 10.0) — CISA KEV-Added 2026-06-11 With First-Ever BOD 26-04 3-Day Federal Deadline Of 2026-06-14; Shadowserver Continues To Report 2/19 Backdoored-To-Vulnerable Internet-Exposed Gateways; Ivanti Disputes Production-Exploitation Framing Calling It 'Honeypot-Only'
findings.affected_technology: Ivanti Sentry (formerly MobileIron Sentry) mobile-gateway — Watchtower has tracked since 2026-06-09 PT-Security dbugs NOTED → 2026-06-10 vendor advisory + watchTowr PoC UPDATE → 2026-06-11 Shadowserver 2/19 backdoored UPDATE; today's material change is CISA's KEV add 2026-06-11 plus first-ever invocation of Binding Operational Directive BOD 26-04 (published 2026-06-11 — see 2026-06-12 NOTED), pinning a 3-day FCEB remediation deadline of Sunday 2026-06-14; per BleepingComputer this is the inaugural use of BOD 26-04 — the directive's 'KEV-listed full-control issue on internet-exposed asset' tier; Shadowserver continues to detect 2/19 internet-exposed gateways already backdoored ('rest likely also compromised') 2026-06-12; Ivanti's official response (SecurityWeek 2026-06-12) reframes the observed exploitation as honeypot-only and reiterates that management port 8443 'should never be exposed to the internet' — a vendor-disputed-framing dynamic to watch given Shadowserver explicitly distinguishes vulnerable-and-backdoored from honeypot signature matches
findings.summary: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 KEV-added 2026-06-11 + first-ever BOD 26-04 invocation pinning 3-day FCEB deadline 2026-06-14 — Shadowserver continues 2/19 internet-exposed-and-backdoored reporting; Ivanti calls it honeypot-only but the same dataset identifies 19 still-vulnerable internet-exposed instances — patch every Sentry to R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1 by Sunday, treat unpatched as already compromised.

findings.title: Arch Linux AUR Mass-Compromise — 400+ Hijacked Packages Push Rust Credential-Stealer + eBPF Kernel Rootkit Via atomic-lockfile@1.4.2 npm Dep In Spoofed-Maintainer PKGBUILD Edits; Harvests Browser / Slack / Discord / Teams Sessions + GitHub / npm / Vault / SSH / Docker Creds; Detection IOCs Published 2026-06-12 By Researcher Whanos, Main Payload SHA-256 6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b
findings.affected_technology: Arch User Repository (AUR) build scripts (PKGBUILD) — 400+ community packages compromised; Arch official repositories not affected; attackers adopted abandoned packages and edited the PKGBUILD files, spoofed git commit metadata to look like long-standing-maintainer commits; the malicious build step pulls atomic-lockfile@1.4.2 from npm during local package build; that npm dep loads a Rust-compiled ELF infostealer that harvests browser cookies / tokens / local storage from Chrome / Edge / Brave, Electron-app session data from Slack / Discord / Microsoft Teams, GitHub credentials / npm tokens / HashiCorp Vault tokens / SSH artefacts, Docker and Podman registry credentials, Telegram session keys; when run with root the payload deploys an eBPF rootkit hiding processes / files / network interfaces that survives conventional cleanup; researcher Whanos has published a detection script + IOC list; main payload SHA-256 6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b; Arch maintainers began removing the malicious commits and banning the offending accounts overnight 2026-06-11/12
findings.summary: Arch Linux AUR mass-compromise — 400+ hijacked packages drop Rust credential-stealer + eBPF rootkit via atomic-lockfile@1.4.2 npm dep in spoofed-maintainer PKGBUILD edits; harvests browser / Slack / Discord / Teams sessions + GitHub / npm / Vault / SSH / Docker creds; rotate every credential on any host that ran makepkg since 2026-06-11 and reimage root-execution hosts because eBPF rootkit removal is unreliable.

findings.title: Agentjacking — New Attack Class Hijacks AI Coding Agents (Claude Code, Cursor) Via Crafted Sentry Error Events Injected At The DSN Ingest Endpoint; 2,388 Organisations With Exposed DSNs Confirmed; 85% Success Rate Across Tested AI Coding Assistants; Sentry Acknowledged + Declined Architectural Fix Calling It 'Not Technically Defensible'
findings.affected_technology: Sentry error-tracking platform event ingestion endpoint + downstream AI coding agents Claude Code and Cursor consuming Sentry data via Model Context Protocol (MCP); Sentry DSNs (Data Source Names) are public, write-only credentials embedded in client-side code so the application can POST error events — Sentry's event-ingestion endpoint accepts arbitrary payloads from anyone holding the DSN; attacker who scrapes a target DSN from public website JavaScript POSTs a maliciously formatted error event whose message and context fields contain markdown that renders identically to legitimate Sentry templates; when a developer asks their AI coding agent to fix unresolved Sentry issues the agent queries Sentry via MCP and interprets the attacker's markdown as trusted system output, executing the embedded instructions with developer-account privileges; Tenet Security reports 85% success rate across tested AI coding assistants and 2,388 organisations with vulnerable DSNs in their published proof-set; bypasses EDR / WAF / IAM / VPN / Cloudflare / host firewalls because the malicious traffic flows over the legitimate Sentry ingest path; Sentry acknowledged + declined architectural fix calling it 'not technically defensible' and shipped a content filter blocking specific payload strings — a stopgap that adversarial markdown can almost certainly evade
findings.summary: Agentjacking — Tenet Security disclosed new attack class hijacking AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor) via crafted Sentry error events posted to public DSN ingest endpoint, 85% success rate against tested agents + 2,388 orgs with exposed DSNs; Sentry declined architectural fix calling it not-technically-defensible — treat all third-party MCP data sources as untrusted input and disable Sentry-MCP integrations on shared projects until structural fix lands.

findings.title: Velvet Ant 'Operation Highland' — China-Nexus APT Backdoored Linux PAM + OpenSSH On Air-Gapped Networks With Nine Modified PAM Modules + Credential-Logging OpenSSH Builds + Secret Master-Password And Logging-Disable Switches; Persistence Dates To 2016 (~Decade-Long Dwell Time); Sygnia Disclosure 2026-06-12
findings.affected_technology: Linux authentication stack on Velvet Ant-targeted enterprise networks — modified /lib/security/pam_*.so modules + custom sshd binary across glibc-based distros; Sygnia researchers published 'Operation Highland' deep-technical report 2026-06-12 of a Chinese state-aligned APT resident inside an air-gapped enterprise network since approximately 2016 evading repeated eradication attempts by backdooring the Linux authentication stack itself; nine separate modified PAM modules + custom sshd build logging credentials + command history + two persistence primitives (hard-coded master password authenticating any user, hidden environment-variable switch disabling credential logging on operator demand); because authentication itself is compromised, traditional containment (password resets / key rotation / session termination) is ineffective; initial-access staging through an internet-facing web server bridge into the air-gapped segment; canonical detection playbook for this attack class: file-integrity-check pam_unix.so / pam_sssd.so / sshd against known-good package baselines, hunt hidden env-variable switches in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/, treat any sshd whose mtime predates last package upgrade as suspect; joins the same group's prior Cisco / F5 / Juniper edge-device zero-day campaigns (Watchtower covered the F5 line in February 2026)
findings.summary: Velvet Ant 'Operation Highland' — Sygnia disclosed ~decade-long China-nexus APT campaign that backdoored Linux PAM (9 modified modules) and OpenSSH (credential-logging build + secret-master-password + logging-disable env switch) on air-gapped enterprise networks since 2016; canonical detection: file-integrity-check pam_*.so + sshd against package hashes — credential rotation alone fails when auth itself is backdoored, re-image any mismatched host.

findings.title: phpBB 10-Year Authentication Bypass — Single-HTTP-Request Login As Any User Including Administrators On Default Configurations Of 3.3.16 And Below + 4.0.0-a2 And Below; Aikido / HackerOne Disclosed 2026-06-02, Patched 3.3.17 Shipped 2026-06-06, Public Disclosure 2026-06-12; ACP RCE Path Blocked By Separate Password Layer But Full-User-Impersonation Reachable
findings.affected_technology: phpBB forum software — 3.3.16 and below + 4.0.0-a2 and below — 10-year-old logic flaw in phpBB authentication allows an unauthenticated attacker to log in as any user, administrator included, with a single HTTP request requiring no special knowledge under default configuration; researchers at Aikido found the bug 2026-06-02 and reported it through phpBB's HackerOne program, phpBB shipped 3.3.17 four days later on 2026-06-06, public disclosure 2026-06-12; remote code execution is not directly reachable because the Admin Control Panel sits behind a separate password-prompt layer, but the bypass yields complete impersonation (read private messages, manipulate content / accounts, deface forums, exfiltrate registered-user PII); no safe 4.x release exists yet — only path is downgrade or wait; corporate exposure surface still non-trivial — community forums attached to mid-market e-commerce brands, internal support portals for legacy products, embedded user-management for industry conferences, partner-portal forums; bypass-as-administrator also makes phpBB instances credible credential-harvesting waterholes for cross-property credential reuse harvesting
findings.summary: phpBB 10-year auth bypass — single-HTTP-request login as any user including administrators on default configurations of 3.3.16 and below + 4.0.0-a2 and below; Aikido found 2026-06-02, patched 3.3.17 shipped 2026-06-06, public disclosure 2026-06-12 — ACP RCE blocked by separate password layer but full impersonation reachable; upgrade 3.x today, no safe 4.x release yet so downgrade or IP allow-list login/ACP endpoints.

findings.title: Squid 7.6 Multi-CVE Batch — CVE-2026-47729 Out-Of-Bounds Read In FTP Gateway (Cross-Session Data Disclosure Primitive) + CVE-2026-50012 Heap Buffer Overflow In Cache Digests Parsing (Malicious-Server Memory-Corruption Primitive, --enable-cache-digests Builds Only); oss-security Disclosure 2026-06-12 By Amos Jeffries / Squid Software Foundation
findings.affected_technology: Squid caching proxy / web cache — patched in Squid 7.6; Amos Jeffries (Squid Software Foundation) disclosed two new Squid CVEs via oss-security 2026-06-12; CVE-2026-47729 out-of-bounds read in FTP gateway component — a legitimate FTP client connecting through Squid against a malicious FTP server can disclose data from unrelated client sessions sharing the same Squid worker process, information-disclosure primitive particularly dangerous for multi-tenant proxy fleets; CVE-2026-50012 heap-based buffer overflow in cache-digests parsing — a malicious upstream cache responding to a cache_digest request can corrupt the Squid worker process's heap, memory-corruption RCE primitive but only when Squid is compiled with --enable-cache-digests (not the most common build flag but non-zero population of enterprise builds enable it for performance reasons); patches linked in the advisory (commits 865a131c7d557e68c965043d98c2eccae26deef8 for FTP, 19fcfe922717c8b255270c032dcde4071c003bcd for cache digests)
findings.summary: Squid 7.6 multi-CVE — CVE-2026-47729 FTP-gateway OOB-read cross-session data disclosure + CVE-2026-50012 heap-overflow in cache_digests parsing (--enable-cache-digests builds only); upgrade Squid to 7.6 across the proxy fleet, recompile without --enable-cache-digests as stopgap, prioritise multi-tenant FTP-gateway-disabled rebuilds.

findings.title: Portainer CVE-2026-33590 (CVSS 8.2) — Insecure Default Settings Allow Regular Portainer Users To Execute Arbitrary Commands With Elevated Privileges On The Container Host (Bind-Mount + Privileged-Mode Defaults); Patched 2.38.0 STS + 2.39.0 LTS By Sifis Bampionitakis / intWave Via oss-security 2026-06-12
findings.affected_technology: Portainer < 2.38.0 STS / < 2.39.0 LTS Docker / Kubernetes container-management UI — ships with insecure default Docker security settings allowing regular Portainer users to spin up containers with bind-mounts of arbitrary host paths + privileged-mode flag set, textbook container-escape-by-design primitive (mount / from host into a privileged container = host root); Sifis Bampionitakis (intWave intern) disclosed via oss-security 2026-06-12; fixed in Portainer 2.38.0 (short-term support) and 2.39.0 (long-term support) by tightening default Docker Security Settings
findings.summary: Portainer CVE-2026-33590 (CVSS 8.2) — insecure defaults let regular Portainer users create privileged + bind-mount containers escaping to host root; patched in 2.38.0 STS and 2.39.0 LTS — upgrade and disable bind-mounts + privileged-mode in Docker Security Settings for all non-admin roles, audit recent container-creation history for surprise privileged + bind-mount-/ containers.

findings.title: LangGraph 3-CVE Chain — CVE-2025-67644 (CVSS 7.3) SQL Injection In SQLite Checkpointer + CVE-2026-28277 (CVSS 6.8) Unsafe msgpack Deserialization + CVE-2026-27022 (CVSS 6.5) RediSearch Query Injection; SQLi + Deser Chain Yields Self-Hosted RCE On Exposed get_state_history(); LangSmith Managed Platform Unaffected
findings.affected_technology: LangGraph (LangChain agentic-framework) self-hosted deployments using SQLite or Redis checkpointers — three checkpointer-store CVEs disclosed 2026-06-12; CVE-2025-67644 (CVSS 7.3) SQLi in SQLite checkpointer via metadata-filter input on get_state_history() endpoint + CVE-2026-28277 (CVSS 6.8) unsafe msgpack deserialization of returned checkpoint blobs combine into arbitrary code execution on the LangGraph server; CVE-2026-27022 (CVSS 6.5) independent RediSearch query-injection in Redis checkpointer allowing access-control bypass on stored agent state; LangSmith's managed platform is not affected — self-hosted-deployment issue only; fix versions langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.0.1+, langgraph 1.0.10+, @langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-redis 1.0.1+; continues the durable pattern from MEMORY 2026-06-11: self-hosted AI workflow / agent platforms (Langflow, Flowise, Open WebUI, FastGPT, now LangGraph) need Web/HTTP-fleet-tier patch SLAs because they expose agent state machinery to attacker input by default
findings.summary: LangGraph 3-CVE chain — CVE-2025-67644 (CVSS 7.3) SQLi in SQLite checkpointer + CVE-2026-28277 (CVSS 6.8) unsafe msgpack deser chain to self-hosted RCE on exposed get_state_history(), plus CVE-2026-27022 (CVSS 6.5) RediSearch query injection in Redis checkpointer — upgrade langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.0.1+ / langgraph 1.0.10+ / langgraph-checkpoint-redis 1.0.1+; LangSmith managed platform unaffected.
